text: Web Access Builder: a spreadsheet and a database, together at last. Design it, then share it with your team, as your own app.

This is a workbook, on a form. Its rows are the records of a database, and the formulas beside them belong to the worksheet. Change a stock level in a cell, and the record is saved at once. Here it is, in the Products form.
Forms work on the same data. This search form builds a filter in VBA, and applies it to the list below.
Queries are designed in a grid: tables, joins and criteria. Run it for the results, or switch to the SQL.
Reports group and total the same data, ready to print, or to save as a PDF.
PivotTable view is here too. Drag a field into the column area, and the totals follow.
The same layout drives a PivotChart. Change the chart type, and it redraws at once.
TreeView controls work too, with drag and drop, through the form's own code.
And VBA runs as VBA, in the browser. Set a breakpoint, click the button on the form, and the code pauses on that line. Step through, then carry on.
There's an assistant too. Ask for what you need, and it shows you its plan. Nothing changes until you say go ahead. Then it builds it, ready to use.
When it's ready, share it. Invite people by email, as a User who works with the data, or a Guest who only reads it.
They get the runtime: your forms and reports, and no design tools. It's free, however many people use it.
Web Access Builder runs on your own desktop, or on a server of your own. Try the demo at webaccessbuilder.com.
